observed_result.criterion: For the selected language (Rust), a non-elevated Windows user can (a) create, persist, reopen in a new process, sign with, and delete an ECDSA P-256 key in the CNG Microsoft Software Key Storage Provider; (b) the same in the Microsoft Platform Crypto Provider (TPM), with the private key non-exportable; (c) DPAPI CurrentUser protect and unprotect across processes. Each signature verifies with the public key the spike exports. Signing latency is measured. The key-name inventory after the run equals the one before. Go is a secondary comparison row with its own verdict.
observed_result.summary: Attempt 3 (run id 3d2d51ca): every Rust check passed. Software KSP: create+finalize 1.8 ms; reopen in a new process 0.47 ms; sign median 114 us (n=20); export policy 0 read back in both processes; ECCPRIVATEBLOB and PKCS8 export refused with 0x80090029. TPM: create+finalize 85 ms; reopen 3.3 ms; sign median 12.5 ms (n=20); export policy 0; private export refused with 0x8009000A NTE_BAD_TYPE; provider Impl Type HARDWARE. Signatures verify with the exported ECCPUBLICBLOB through BCrypt in a separate process and through OpenSSL 4.1.0 on the Mac; tampered signatures and a wrong digest are rejected. Delete reopens as NTE_BAD_KEYSET. DPAPI CurrentUser works across processes: protect median 187 us, unprotect median 147 us. Go (unmodified) passed DPAPI in-process and Software KSP create/duplicate/sign-in-new-process/delete, and TPM create/duplicate/sign-in-new-process. Its TPM delete failed with 0x80090009 NTE_BAD_FLAGS because the spike passes NCRYPT_SILENT_FLAG; the runner sweep deleted that key by exact name with the Rust binary. The Rust spike had the same defect in attempt 2, which left two TPM test keys; the fix (dwFlags = 0 on NTE_BAD_FLAGS) was applied, the two keys were deleted by exact name, and attempt 3 ran cleanly. Inventory: software KSP 60 names (sha256 02c84226...) and PCP 2 names (sha256 4305099e...) before and after attempt 3, equal to the preflight and to the final check at 23:04:49Z; no key with the run prefix remains (spike enumeration and certutil).

product_findings: On the Platform Crypto Provider, NCryptDeleteKey must be called with dwFlags = 0: NCRYPT_SILENT_FLAG returns NTE_BAD_FLAGS there, while the Software KSP accepts it.
NCRYPT_IMPL_TYPE_PROPERTY is not supported on key handles in either provider (0x80090029); read it from the provider handle (software 0x22, platform 0x1).
TPM signing costs about 12.5 ms per ECDSA P-256 signature on this AMD fTPM, versus about 0.11 ms with the Software KSP; TPM key creation about 85 ms.

limitations: One native host, one user, one current run (attempt 3), plus attempt 2 for repeat values. The TPM is an AMD firmware TPM (revision 1.59); discrete TPMs and Pluton are untested.

Lock, sign-out, sleep and reboot are out of scope (P-W1/P-W2: g04-windows-desktop-lock-probe.json and g04-windows-signout-reboot-probe.json stay blocked). No second account, so cross-user isolation of keys and DPAPI blobs is untested.
The private-export refusal has no positive control: no exportable key was created to show that the same call succeeds when export is allowed.

Software KSP non-exportability is a policy enforced by the provider. The key material stays in the user profile under the user's DPAPI protection, so same-user code with profile access is a residual risk [I, not tested]. That TPM key material never leaves the TPM in clear comes from vendor documentation, not from a test.

Go coverage is narrower (source unmodified): no export policy readback, no private-export attempt, no public-key verification, no in-process timing, no cross-process DPAPI. Its TPM delete fails on the NCRYPT_SILENT_FLAG defect; a Go fix was not tested.

The spike and the runner changed after results were seen: the attempt-1 runner variable fix, and the attempt-2 to 3 delete-flag and provider Impl Type changes. The criterion did not change. The diffs are kept.

The inventory compares the current user's key names only: count, SHA-256 of the sorted names, and run-prefix names. It does not compare other keys' properties or material, and it does not cover machine keys (none were created). The certutil cross-check counts run-prefix lines only.
Timings are single-run, warm, with 20 samples (std::time::Instant); process wall times include PowerShell Start-Process overhead. Not a benchmark.

A preflight log line was corrected: my first certutil preflight command echoed a hard-coded 'heimdall_lines=0' that was not measured. I removed those lines and re-ran the command with a measured count (0 and 0), which is what the log keeps.
The console screen was not observed. 'No prompt' rests on NCRYPT_SILENT_FLAG/CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN plus short process times.
